story.title: Trump Announces Deal for Hamas Disarmament and Israeli Withdrawal from Gaza
story.summary: President Trump has announced a deal for Hamas to completely disarm, which includes the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. Hamas confirmed its agreement to the plan, stating it would hand over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee. However, the implementation of this deal is contingent upon Israel fulfilling its commitments from a previous agreement.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed in this announcement?
explore_lenses.title: A roadmap agreement, not completed disarmament
explore_lenses.summary: The new element is an agreed roadmap for Gaza’s next ceasefire phase: Hamas and other factions would transfer governance and ultimately weapons control to a Palestinian technocratic body, while Israeli withdrawal would proceed in linked phases. The published text does not mean Hamas has already surrendered its arsenal or that Israel has already withdrawn.

claims.text: The roadmap says Hamas and other factions will hand civilian governance and security functions to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), which is to operate independently during the transition.
Police weapons are to transfer to NCAG when it enters Gaza, but heavy weapons, weapons depots, military-production sites and tunnels are assigned to a later decommissioning process.
Hamas official Bassem Naim confirmed that the group agreed to the deal, according to AP; the agreement ties its implementation to Israeli steps including an end to hostilities and withdrawal.

explore_lenses.label: What must happen before withdrawal begins?
explore_lenses.title: Verification, NCAG entry and phased implementation
explore_lenses.summary: The text establishes a sequence rather than an immediate exchange of weapons for withdrawal. A new international verification body must first certify compliance, and the NCAG and an international stabilization force are prerequisites for the heavy-weapons process.

claims.text: Within 14 days after all parties approve the roadmap, they are to prepare the Phase 2 timetable and implementation mechanisms; the proposed International Verification Committee may extend that period.

The International Verification Committee, to be established by the Board of Peace and including guarantors, the Board and the International Stabilization Force, is tasked with certifying compliance before Phase 2 proceeds and monitoring violations.

The agreement says decommissioning of heavy weapons and military infrastructure begins only after remaining prior commitments are completed, NCAG enters Gaza and the International Stabilization Force deploys; it is linked to phased Israeli withdrawal.
A Board of Peace official told AP the heavy-weapons and infrastructure process could take 200 to 350 days, but that timeframe is not included in the published agreement.

explore_lenses.label: Where do Hamas and Israel still differ?
explore_lenses.title: Sequencing and control of weapons remain disputed
explore_lenses.summary: Hamas frames disarmament as conditional on reciprocal Israeli commitments and Palestinian custody of weapons. Israeli officials had publicly maintained that full demilitarization must precede withdrawal, while Israel had not formally commented on the announced roadmap.

claims.text: Hamas negotiator Ghazi Hamad said the Palestinian National Committee, rather than Israel, would undertake disarmament; Hamas said it expected mediators and the Board of Peace to ensure Israel complied with withdrawal terms.
The roadmap specifies that weapons are to be stored under NCAG authority and says no weapons will be transferred or handed to Israel or other non-Palestinian parties.

Before the announcement, an Israeli political source said Israel demanded complete disarmament, removal of weapons from Gaza and full demilitarization as a precondition for any process; AP separately reported Israel had issued no formal response to the deal.
Board of Peace high representative Nickolay Mladenov said implementation and verification must be real and that withdrawal must move “in lockstep” with decommissioning.

story_report.summary: President Trump announced an agreement under which Hamas would disarm and Israeli forces would gradually withdraw from Gaza. Hamas official Bassem Naim confirmed that the group had agreed, but tied implementation to Israeli actions including ending hostilities and withdrawing. The roadmap would shift civilian governance and security functions from Hamas and other factions to an independent Palestinian administration during a transition, making the proposed handover contingent on reciprocal steps rather than an immediate transfer of all weapons.

sections.heading: Gaza Administration Would Assume Security
sections.body: The roadmap assigns civilian governance and security responsibilities to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, or NCAG, which is intended to operate independently during the transition. Police weapons are to transfer to NCAG when it enters Gaza. Heavy weapons, stockpiles, military-production facilities and tunnels, however, are designated for a later decommissioning process, while the weapons are to be stored under NCAG authority rather than handed to Israel or another non-Palestinian party.

sections.heading: Verification Governs Phased Withdrawal Process
sections.body: After all parties approve the roadmap, they are to prepare a Phase 2 timetable and implementation mechanisms within 14 days, subject to a possible extension by a proposed International Verification Committee. The committee, to include guarantors, the Board of Peace and the International Stabilization Force, would certify compliance before Phase 2 and monitor violations. Heavy-weapons and military-infrastructure decommissioning would begin only after prior commitments are completed, NCAG enters Gaza and the stabilization force deploys, alongside a phased Israeli withdrawal.

sections.heading: Israel and Hamas Differ on Disarmament
sections.body: Hamas negotiator Ghazi Hamad said a Palestinian national committee, rather than Israel, would carry out the disarmament, and said Hamas expected mediators and the Board of Peace to ensure Israel met withdrawal terms. Before the announcement, an Israeli political source said Israel required complete disarmament, removal of weapons from Gaza and full demilitarization before any process. Board of Peace representative Nickolay Mladenov said verification must be genuine and that withdrawal should proceed “in lockstep” with decommissioning.

unresolved.text: The published roadmap does not establish that weapons have been collected, tunnels dismantled or an Israeli withdrawal timetable agreed.
Neither the final implementation timetable nor the date NCAG would enter Gaza was public as of July 31, 2026.
Israel’s formal acceptance of the roadmap, including how it would interpret sequencing and verification requirements, remained unresolved.

related_stories.title: Trump Indicates No Objection to Withdrawing Todd Blanche's Nomination Amid Senate Delays
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump has stated he has 'no objection' to withdrawing Todd Blanche's nomination for Attorney General. This comes as two Republican senators, Thom Tillis and John Cornyn, are withholding support, leading to a delay in the Senate vote. The senators are seeking a written commitment from the Department of Justice regarding a disputed compensation fund that could benefit Trump allies.

related_stories.title: Mandela Barnes Exits Wisconsin Governor Democratic Primary
related_stories.summary: Mandela Barnes has announced his withdrawal from the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor. The former lieutenant governor shared the news in a video on social media. His departure comes amid reports of an investigation into allegations regarding his conduct within the state Democratic party.

related_stories.title: Fauci Faces Contempt Threats After Invoking Fifth Amendment in Senate Hearing
related_stories.summary: Dr. Anthony Fauci has faced backlash from Republican lawmakers after he invoked his Fifth Amendment right during a Senate hearing regarding the COVID pandemic. This has raised concerns about potential contempt of Congress charges, despite Fauci having received a pardon.

related_stories.title: Spain's Sánchez Attributes Migrant Surge to Trafficking Gangs in Ceuta
related_stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has attributed the recent influx of approximately 60,000 migrants to Ceuta to trafficking gangs. He criticized these criminal networks for misleading migrants regarding a recent court ruling that affects the immediate return of those arriving by sea. Sánchez described the situation as a violation of Spain's national territory and emphasized the need for a coordinated response to the crisis.
